html:
Nader Shah's invasion of India was a campaign in 1738 and 1739 in which the Persian king Nader Shah defeated the Mughal Empire, sacked Delhi and carried off a great treasure.

Nader had pushed through Afghanistan and into the Punjab. After his victory at Karnal in February 1739 he entered Delhi. A rumour that he had been killed started a riot in which some of his soldiers died. In reply he ordered a massacre of the city's people, in which tens of thousands were killed, and then looted the treasury and palaces.

He took the Peacock Throne, the Koh-i-Noor and an immense amount of coin, and left after about two months, restoring the Mughal emperor but keeping lands west of the Indus. The raid made the Mughals even weaker and left the north open to Afghan and Maratha rivals.
sum: Nader Shah's invasion of India was a campaign in 1738 and 1739 in which the Persian king Nader Shah defeated the Mughal Empire, sacked Delhi and carried off a great treasure.
